sections.section_title: Foundations of Transcatheter Valve Reintervention and Endocarditis
sections.description: This section establishes the necessary background knowledge regarding the evolution of TAVI, the mechanisms of structural valve deterioration, and the specific pathophysiology of prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE). It prepares the reader to understand the unique challenges of treating patients with prior transcatheter implants and active or resolved infections.
subtopics: Evolution of TAVI indications and long-term survival trends
Pathophysiology of structural valve deterioration (SVD) in bioprostheses
Clinical presentation and complications of prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE)
Indications and contraindications for transcatheter valve-in-valve procedures
Anatomical risks of serial reinterventions (coronary obstruction, patient-prosthesis mismatch)

sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Comprehensive Diagnostic Workup
sections.description: This section details the patient's clinical history, symptomatology, and the multimodal diagnostic approach required to assess valve function and infection status. It emphasizes the critical role of imaging in characterizing complex multi-prosthesis anatomy.
subtopics: Patient demographics, comorbidities, and surgical risk profile
Symptom assessment: Dyspnea, heart failure, and functional capacity
Echocardiographic evaluation of prosthetic valve gradients and regurgitation
Multislice CT (MSCT) planning: Frame interaction, coronary height, and lumen diameter
Criteria for confirming resolution of infective endocarditis prior to intervention

sections.description: This section explains the clinical reasoning process used by the Heart Team to select a third TAVI over surgical replacement. It covers the balancing of prohibitive surgical risk against the technical feasibility of a triple-stented configuration in a post-endocarditis patient.
subtopics: Surgical vs. transcatheter risk assessment (EuroSCORE II and Heart Team consensus)
Timing of intervention relative to antibiotic therapy and infection clearance
Evaluation of coronary obstruction risk in triple-valve anatomy
Mitigation strategies for patient-prosthesis mismatch (PPM)
Rationale for valve selection (Acurate neo2) based on anatomical constraints

sections.description: This section provides a step-by-step breakdown of the TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV procedure, focusing on the specific technical maneuvers employed to ensure safety and efficacy. It highlights the integration of preprocedural imaging into real-time execution.
subtopics: Vascular access strategies and hemodynamic monitoring
Balloon pre-dilation and coronary flow verification
Commissural alignment techniques to preserve future coronary access
High implantation strategy to prevent neo-skirt obstruction
Post-dilation optimization for frame expansion and leaflet mobility

sections.section_title: Clinical Outcomes, Follow-up, and Lifetime Management Lessons
sections.description: This section reviews the immediate and long-term outcomes of the intervention, analyzing hemodynamic improvements and complication rates. It concludes with broader clinical lessons regarding the lifetime management of structural valve disease in the era of increasing TAVI longevity.
subtopics: Immediate procedural success and hemodynamic parameters (gradients, AVA, DVI)
Short-term and 1-year follow-up data on valve function and symptoms
Resolution of patient-prosthesis mismatch over time
Surveillance strategies for serial transcatheter prostheses
Future considerations: Surgical explantation risks and emerging catheter-based solutions
